Skill loaded successfully ✅

# Research Workspace Manager

Load the host-specific research environment, reuse known assets, and apply the
canonical research workspace lifecycle to:

**$ARGUMENTS**

This is the only skill the user needs to invoke for local research. It combines
VM storage management, asset discovery, paper organization, project layout,
idea lifecycle, attempt tracking, run allocation, result persistence, and
catalog maintenance.

This skill is specific to the Azure VM `xasi-agent-training`. Use absolute paths
throughout. The persistent source of truth is:

`/data/results/README.md`

## 1. Mandatory preflight

Run this before reading, downloading, generating, or moving large assets:

```bash
/data/results/copilot-skills/research-workspace-manager/scripts/preflight.sh
```

The preflight must confirm:

- `/scratch` is an XFS mount backed by `/dev/md0`.
- `/dev/md0` is the active four-NVMe RAID0 array.
- `/scratch/assets` exists.
- The persistent catalogs under `/data/results/catalog` are readable.
- Sufficient free capacity exists for the requested operation.

If `/scratch` is missing or resolves to the root filesystem, **stop**. Do not
create a replacement `/scratch/assets` directory on the OS disk. Do not
format, recreate, or repair the RAID without explicit user approval.

## 2. Durability boundary

| Absolute location | Durability | Required use |
|---|---|---|
| `/home/user` | Persistent managed OS disk | Code, Git repositories, virtual environments, user configuration |
| `/data` | Persistent managed data disk | Catalogs, papers, final results, reports, plots, irreplaceable checkpoints |
| `/scratch/assets` | Ephemeral local NVMe RAID0 | Datasets, model weights, reusable caches, intermediate checkpoints, temporary working data |

`/scratch` can be erased by VM stop/deallocate, redeploy, host migration, or one
failed RAID0 member. Never leave the only copy of an irreplaceable artifact
there.

## 3. Environment constants

Use these exact paths even if the current parent process has stale environment
variables:

```bash
export RESEARCH_HUB=/data/results
export RESEARCH_ASSETS=/scratch/assets
export HF_HOME=/scratch/assets/huggingface
```

They are also configured in `/home/user/.bashrc`. The persistent
Hugging Face credential is stored at
`/home/user/.config/huggingface/token`; never print, catalog, copy to a
repository, or expose its contents.

Convenience links:

- `/home/user/research-assets` -> `/scratch/assets`
- `/scratch/datasets` -> `/scratch/assets/datasets`
- `/scratch/models` -> `/scratch/assets/models`
- `/scratch/cache` -> `/scratch/assets/caches`
- `/scratch/checkpoints` -> `/scratch/assets/checkpoints`
- `/scratch/work` -> `/scratch/assets/work`
- `/scratch/tmp` -> `/scratch/assets/tmp`

## 4. Always search before downloading

The catalogs are authoritative. Search them before any network download:

```bash
rg -i '<name|alias|topic>' /data/results/catalog/ASSETS.tsv
rg -i '<title|arxiv-id|topic>' /data/results/catalog/PAPERS.tsv
rg -i '<venue|year|author-kit|policy>' /data/results/catalog/VENUE_RESOURCES.tsv
rg -i '<repo|project|origin>' /data/results/catalog/WORKSPACES.tsv
```

Catalog meanings:

- `/data/results/catalog/ASSETS.tsv`: datasets, models, Hugging Face
  collections, reusable caches, sizes, and compatibility paths.
- `/data/results/catalog/PAPERS.tsv`: every known PDF, SHA-256, title,
  topic, document kind, source, and topic-library link.
- `/data/results/catalog/VENUE_RESOURCES.tsv`: official author kits,
  venue policies, templates, and dated web snapshots.
- `/data/results/catalog/PAPER_PACKAGES.tsv`: durable Stage 4 manuscript
  packages linked to their Project, Idea, and Attempt.
- `/data/results/catalog/WORKSPACES.tsv`: known Git repositories, branches,
  commits, and origins.
- `/data/results/catalog/MIGRATION_MAP.tsv`: legacy path to canonical
  asset mapping.
- `/data/results/catalog/audit/files-pre-migration.tsv.gz`: complete
  pre-migration file inventory for difficult lookups.

After a catalog match, inspect the canonical path and reuse it. Do not copy an
asset into a project merely for convenience; create a symbolic link if the
project requires a local-looking path.

## 5. Existing canonical assets

### Datasets

- `/scratch/assets/datasets/tabular/rl-pt-table`
  - Main table reasoning, spreadsheet, and text-to-SQL datasets.
- `/scratch/assets/datasets/benchmarks/migrated-datasets`
  - Agent and language-model benchmarks migrated from project-local storage.
- `/scratch/assets/datasets/retrieval/prefix-kv-calibration`
  - Prefix/KV, retrieval, and RAG experiment data.
- `/scratch/assets/datasets/tabular/tef-pilot-raw`
  - TEF pilot raw tabular data.
- `/scratch/assets/huggingface/datasets`
  - Processed Hugging Face dataset cache.
- `/scratch/assets/huggingface/hub/datasets--*`
  - Hugging Face dataset download repositories.

### Models

- `/scratch/assets/models/manual/agent-related-learning`
  - Manually downloaded Qwen3, Gemma, and related weights.
- `/scratch/assets/models/manual/tef-pilot`
  - TEF pilot model weights, including Qwen2.5-Coder-32B.
- `/scratch/assets/huggingface/hub/models--*`
  - Shared Hugging Face model cache.
- `/scratch/assets/caches/models`
  - Reusable project model caches.

### Reusable caches

- `/scratch/assets/caches/experiments/prefix-kv-calibration`
  - Large prefix/KV experiment caches.
- `/scratch/assets/caches/models/tooldisentangle`
- `/scratch/assets/caches/models/chronopolicy`
- `/scratch/assets/caches/retrieval/boundary-transfer`

The catalog, not this summary, is the source of truth as assets evolve.

## 6. Existing persistent workspaces

Keep these repositories at their current absolute locations:

- `/home/user/Agent-Related-Learning`
- `/home/user/microsoft_research_studio`
- `/home/user/AutoResearchClaw`
- `/home/user/AgentVBenchmark_Contribute`
- `/home/user/aris_repo`
- `/home/user/prefix-kv-calibration`
- `/data/prefix-kv-calibration`
- `/data/tef-pilot`
- `/data/llm-understand-tabular-data`
- `/data/azureuser/RL_PT_table`

Do not relocate existing repositories or rewrite their internal asset paths
without a task-specific reason. Existing legacy paths are compatibility links
to the canonical NVMe assets.

Place a new repository under:

`/home/user/research-workspaces/<topic>/<repository-name>`

Keep its virtual environment at:

`/home/user/research-workspaces/<topic>/<repository-name>/.venv`

Never clone repositories, install environments, or create code worktrees under
`/scratch` solely for speed. Script and import speed gains are negligible;
durability and stable paths matter more.

## 7. Canonical research entity model

Every managed research effort uses exactly four nested entities:

`Project -> Idea -> Attempt -> Run`

- **Project:** one durable code repository or workspace.
- **Idea:** one stable research hypothesis or direction. Never copy it into
  `idea_2`, `final-idea`, or another directory for a retry.
- **Attempt:** one implementation or methodological revision of an Idea.
- **Run:** one executable configuration, seed, or evaluation invocation.

Status belongs in metadata, not directory names.

### IDs

- Project: stable lowercase slug, for example `agent-evaluation`.
- Idea: `I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-slug`.
- Attempt: `ANNN-short-slug`.
- Run: `R-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` with optional collision suffix and optional `-s<seed>`.

Forbidden ad hoc names include `_2`, `final-final`, `attempt_new`,
`test-tmp-round4`, and status words encoded as directory copies.

## 8. Canonical project layout

Managed projects keep code and research control files on persistent storage:

```text
<project-root>/
├── src/
├── scripts/
├── configs/
├── tests/
├── third_party/
└── .research/
    ├── PROJECT.yaml
    ├── INDEX.tsv
    ├── inbox/
    ├── ideas/
    │   └── I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-slug/
    │       ├── idea.yaml
    │       ├── README.md
    │       ├── proposal/
    │       ├── literature/
    │       ├── plan/
    │       ├── reviews/
    │       │   ├── external/
    │       │   └── audits/
    │       ├── attempts/
    │       │   └── ANNN-short-slug/
    │       │       ├── attempt.yaml
    │       │       ├── implementation/
    │       │       ├── configs/
    │       │       └── runs/
    │       └── decision/
    ├── promoted/
    └── archive/
        ├── rejected/
        ├── paused/
        └── superseded/
```

The project root must remain on `/home/user` or `/data`, never on
`/scratch`.

Use the deterministic helper instead of manually inventing directories. `workspace_manager.py` serializes Idea/Attempt/Run allocation with the catalog lock and retries on collisions, so concurrent callers must use the helper rather than precomputing IDs:

```bash
MANAGER=/data/results/copilot-skills/research-workspace-manager/scripts/workspace_manager.py

python3 "$MANAGER" init-project \
  --root /absolute/persistent/project/path \
  --project project-slug

python3 "$MANAGER" create-idea \
  --root /absolute/persistent/project/path \
  --slug short-idea-slug \
  --title "Human-readable title"

python3 "$MANAGER" create-attempt \
  --idea /absolute/path/to/I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-idea-slug \
  --slug baseline

python3 "$MANAGER" create-run \
  --attempt /absolute/path/to/ANNN-baseline \
  --seed 13

python3 "$MANAGER" set-idea-status \
  --idea /absolute/path/to/I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-idea-slug \
  --status promoted

python3 "$MANAGER" set-attempt-status \
  --attempt /absolute/path/to/ANNN-baseline \
  --status evaluated

python3 "$MANAGER" set-run-status \
  --final /data/results/results/<project>/<idea>/<attempt>/<run> \
  --status succeeded

python3 "$MANAGER" summary --root /absolute/persistent/project/path
```


For Auto Research portfolio/GPU windows, derive deterministic sidecar window IDs with the stage-local helper:

```bash
python3 /data/results/copilot-skills/auto_research-stage-2-skill/scripts/portfolio_ledger.py window-id \
  --project-id <project> --idea-id <idea> --attempt-id <attempt> [--run-id <run>]
```

### Lifecycle states

Idea:

`inbox, scoped, planned, piloting, evaluating, promoted, rejected, paused, superseded`

Attempt:

`planned, implementing, running, evaluated, selected, rejected, paused`

Run:

`allocated, queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled`

Paper package:

`allocated, drafting, reviewing, ready_for_stage5, stage5_reviewing,
stage5_experimenting, stage5_revising, ready_for_submission, blocked_stage5,
failed, cancelled`

Retries create a new Attempt or Run, not a copied Idea directory.

## 9. Run storage contract

For each Run, the manager allocates:

```text
/scratch/assets/work/<project>/<idea>/<attempt>/<run>/
├── logs/
├── checkpoints/
├── predictions/
└── intermediate/

/data/results/results/<project>/<idea>/<attempt>/<run>/
├── run.yaml
├── reports/
├── figures/
└── final-checkpoint/
```

The Attempt's `runs/<run-id>` entry is a symbolic link to the persistent result
directory. The scratch path is recorded in `run.yaml`.

High-volume intermediate data belongs on scratch. Exact configuration, command,
seed, metrics, reports, figures, audit logs, and irreplaceable checkpoints must
be persisted under the result directory before a Run is complete.

## 10. Global research catalogs

The manager owns these persistent TSV catalogs:

- `/data/results/catalog/PROJECTS.tsv`
- `/data/results/catalog/IDEAS.tsv`
- `/data/results/catalog/ATTEMPTS.tsv`
- `/data/results/catalog/RUNS.tsv`

Do not edit them without acquiring
`/data/results/catalog/.catalog.lock`. Idea/Attempt/Run allocation also uses this lock plus collision retry to keep catalogs and directories consistent under concurrency. Prefer the manager helper for all
updates. These are indexes only; they must not duplicate payloads.

## 11. Legacy project handling

Existing trees may contain `ideaspark_run`, `phase0`, `phase1`, `attempt_1`,
`implementation`, `audit`, `review-stage`, `workspace/ideas`, or
`workspace/experiments`.

Do not reorganize a legacy tree merely because this skill was invoked. For new
work inside a legacy project:

1. Initialize `<project-root>/.research`.
2. Allocate the new Idea with the manager.
3. Link relevant legacy files from the managed Idea if needed.
4. Keep old phase directories unchanged until the user explicitly requests a
   migration.
5. During an approved migration, retain raw phase material under
   `<idea>/legacy/` and record its source path.

| Legacy | Managed structure |
|---|---|
| `ideaspark_run/<slug>` | `research/ideas/<idea-id>` |
| `phase0...phase4` | `proposal/`, `literature/`, `plan/`, or `legacy/` |
| `attempt_1` | `attempts/A001-*` |
| `implementation` | `attempts/<attempt>/implementation` |
| `review-stage`, `reviews` | `reviews/external` |
| `audit`, `audits` | `reviews/audits` |
| `test-tmp-*` | scratch temporary Run data |
| accepted paper work | promoted Idea plus persistent paper directory |

## 12. Placement rules for new assets

### Hugging Face

Use `HF_HOME=/scratch/assets/huggingface`. Do not pass a project-local
cache directory. If a tool requires `local_dir`, first verify that a cached
snapshot cannot be reused.

### Manual model download

Use:

`/scratch/assets/models/manual/<provider>/<model-name>`

Download to a sibling `.partial` path, validate size/checksum, then atomically
rename it. Never overwrite an existing model directory without checking its
revision and catalog record.

### Dataset

Use:

`/scratch/assets/datasets/<topic>/<dataset-name>`

Recommended topics include `tabular`, `text2sql`, `retrieval`, `agents`,
`coding`, `reasoning`, `multimodal`, and `benchmarks`.

### Derived cache

Use:

`/scratch/assets/caches/<cache-type>/<project-or-method>`

Examples of cache types: `experiments`, `models`, `retrieval`, `embeddings`,
`tokenized`, and `compiled`.

### Temporary experiment data

Use:

`/scratch/assets/work/<project>/<run-id>`

Use a stable run ID such as `<method>-<dataset>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>`.

## 13. Experiment output contract

For every substantial run, define both:

```bash
RUN_ID='<method>-<dataset>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>'
SCRATCH_RUN="/scratch/assets/work/<project>/$RUN_ID"
FINAL_RUN="/data/results/results/<project>/$RUN_ID"
```

Write high-volume temporary outputs and intermediate checkpoints to
`$SCRATCH_RUN`. Persist these to `$FINAL_RUN`:

- Exact configuration and command line
- Seeds and environment/package metadata
- Final metrics and evaluation outputs
- Logs needed to audit the result
- Plots, tables, reports, and paper-ready figures
- Best/final checkpoints that cannot be cheaply regenerated

Copy and verify final artifacts before deleting temporary data. During long
runs, sync an irreplaceable checkpoint after each major evaluation or epoch.
Never report an experiment complete while its only result copy is on
`/scratch`.

## 14. Paper management

Search `/data/results/catalog/PAPERS.tsv` by title, arXiv ID, DOI, and
topic before downloading. This is a per-paper requirement. Auto Research and
other calling skills must not reduce manager use to `init-project`.

Use the manager commands rather than manually appending catalog rows:

```bash
MANAGER=/data/results/copilot-skills/research-workspace-manager/scripts/workspace_manager.py

python3 "$MANAGER" paper-search --query '<title|doi|arxiv-id|topic>' --json

python3 "$MANAGER" register-paper \
  --source-pdf /scratch/assets/tmp/<run>/<paper>.pdf.partial \
  --topic tabular-and-text2sql \
  --title 'Paper title' \
  --paper-id '<doi-or-arxiv-id>' \
  --source-url 'https://...' \
  --license '<license-or-access-basis>'
```

`register-paper` validates the PDF, computes SHA-256, reuses an existing
cataloged reference by content when possible, atomically stores new reusable
papers under `/data/results/papers/library/<topic>/`, creates the
`papers/by-topic/` link and persistent metadata sidecar, and updates
`PAPERS.tsv` under the catalog lock. Callers must use the returned
`canonical_path`, `sha256`, and `topic_link`; a connector's session-local output
is only a temporary input.

For a paper tied to one project, keep the original PDF in that project's
persistent paper directory. For a general reusable reference, use:

`/data/results/papers/library/<topic>/<paper-name>.pdf`

Create a topic link under:

`/data/results/papers/by-topic/<topic>/<sha12>__<paper-name>.pdf`

Supported topic names:

- `agents-and-research`
- `causality-and-attribution`
- `foundation-models`
- `quantization`
- `retrieval-memory-and-kv`
- `systems-and-efficiency`
- `tabular-and-text2sql`
- `other`

Do not classify generated figures, compiled project drafts, CVs, or package
resources as reference papers. Legacy catalog maintenance may still preserve
non-reference kinds, but new literature retrieval uses `register-paper`.

### 14.1 Venue resources

Search before downloading an author kit, template, policy, or submission page:

```bash
python3 "$MANAGER" venue-resource-search --query 'AAAI 2027' --json
```

Download a missing resource to a `.partial` file under
`/scratch/assets/tmp/<transaction-id>/`, validate it, then register it:

```bash
python3 "$MANAGER" register-venue-resource \
  --source-file /scratch/assets/tmp/<transaction-id>/AuthorKit27.zip.partial \
  --venue AAAI --year 2027 --resource-kind author-kit \
  --title 'AAAI-27 Author Kit' \
  --source-url 'https://aaai.org/authorkit27/' \
  --license 'official author resource' \
  --extract
```

The manager atomically stores the resource under
`/data/results/venue-resources/<venue>/<year>/<resource-kind>/`, rejects
unsafe ZIP members, writes a metadata receipt, and updates
`VENUE_RESOURCES.tsv`. Never register API keys, cookies, access tokens, or
private submission content as venue resources.

### 14.2 Stage 4 paper packages

Paper writing does not create a new Idea or experimental Run. It reuses the
Stage 3 Idea and full-validation Attempt, then allocates a manuscript package:

```bash
python3 "$MANAGER" create-paper-package \
  --attempt /absolute/path/to/<idea>/attempts/<attempt> \
  --venue AAAI-27
```

The returned durable package has this layout:

```text
/data/results/papers/projects/<project>/<idea>/<attempt>/<package-id>/
├── package.json
├── paper/
├── reviews/
│   ├── writing/
│   └── visual-format/
├── audits/
├── handoff/
└── snapshots/
```

Use `set-paper-package-status` for
`allocated -> drafting -> reviewing -> ready_for_stage5`. Before the ready
transition, persist `paper/main.pdf`, `paper/main.tex`, both reviewer summary
JSON files, `handoff/STAGE4_TERMINAL.json`, and
`handoff/HANDOFF_TO_STAGE5.json`, then run:

```bash
python3 "$MANAGER" validate-paper-package \
  --package <absolute-package-path> --require-ready-artifacts
```

The package is a durable presentation artifact, not evidence of scientific
acceptance. Stage 5 remains responsible for technical review.

### 14.3 Stage 5 technical-review package

Stage 5 reuses the Stage 4 `PaperPackage`. It writes only under `stage5/` and
updates the package status:

```text
ready_for_stage5
  -> stage5_reviewing
  -> stage5_experimenting (only when evidence repair is required)
  -> stage5_revising
  -> ready_for_submission | blocked_stage5
```

Reviewer-requested executable work is not hidden inside the paper package.
Create a new hypothesis-preserving Attempt under the same Idea and allocate one
Run per configuration/seed/evaluation. Persist the new Attempt/Run binding and
evidence addendum under `stage5/experiments/`.

Before `ready_for_submission`, Stage 5 must persist its terminal, final
meta-review, acceptance-robustness report, panel history, issue ledger,
result-reporting audit, submission-readiness report, and final audit bundle.
Then run:

```bash
python3 "$MANAGER" validate-paper-package \
  --package <absolute-package-path> \
  --require-ready-artifacts \
  --require-stage5-artifacts
```

`ready_for_submission` means the local calibrated panel and deterministic
gates passed. It is not a guarantee that an external venue will accept.

## 15. Asset catalog update contract

After adding an asset, update
`/data/results/catalog/ASSETS.tsv` using its existing schema:

`category, collection, name, canonical_path, compatibility_path, bytes, files, notes`

Requirements:

1. Acquire `/data/results/catalog/.catalog.lock` with `flock` while
   modifying a catalog.
2. Preserve the header and tab-separated format.
3. Use an absolute canonical path.
4. Record source URL, provider/revision, license, and checksum in `notes` when
   known.
5. Compute actual bytes and file count from the completed asset.
6. Do not add credentials, tokens, private keys, or secret values.
7. Do not add a duplicate row for the same canonical path.

After cloning a repository, add/update
`/data/results/catalog/WORKSPACES.tsv`. After adding a PDF, update
`/data/results/catalog/PAPERS.tsv`. Register venue kits and policies in
`VENUE_RESOURCES.tsv`; register Stage 4 manuscript packages in
`PAPER_PACKAGES.tsv`.

## 16. Auto Research caller contract

The Auto Research skills call this manager automatically. Users do not need to
invoke the manager separately. Calling skills must treat the manager as the
authority for storage and entity identity, not as a one-time initialization
helper.

### 16.1 Required startup transaction

Every stage invocation or resume performs this exact sequence:

1. Read this entire skill and `/data/results/README.md`.
2. Run `preflight.sh` and persist its complete receipt in the stage run.
3. Resolve the persistent Project from `PROJECTS.tsv` and `.research/PROJECT.yaml`.
4. Initialize the Project only when no managed Project exists.
5. Query live catalogs again on resume; never rely on a copied stage summary.

If preflight, the helper, a catalog, or the persistent Project is unavailable,
the stage is blocked. Do not silently fall back to a session directory, `/tmp`,
scratch, or manually invented metadata.

### 16.2 Paper transaction for Stage 1 and fresh collision searches

For every paper selected for full-text inspection:

1. Run `paper-search --query <stable-id> --json`, then normalized title/alias
   searches when needed.
2. Reuse a matching reference only after verifying source PDF, SHA-256, and
   topic link.
3. Otherwise download to a `.partial` file under
   `/scratch/assets/tmp/<stage-run-id>/`.
4. Run `register-paper` and parse its JSON output.
5. Persist exactly the returned `registration_status`, `paper_id`, `sha256`,
   `canonical_path`, `topic_link`, and `metadata_path`.
6. Verify the canonical artifact, then delete the partial or stray connector
   copy.

The manager output is a receipt. A calling skill must not reconstruct paths,
hand-write a `PAPERS.tsv` row, or treat a successful network download as a
successful paper transaction.

### 16.3 Stage 2 entity transaction

Cheap sketches and paper-only audits remain in the Project's Stage 2 inbox.
When a finalist is independently accepted for executable pilot work:

1. `create-idea` once for the stable hypothesis.
2. `create-attempt` for the pilot implementation/revision.
3. `create-run` for every executable baseline, metric sanity check, direct
   test, discriminator, retry, and confirmation.
4. Set each Run to `running`, then to its actual terminal status.
5. Persist result evidence under the Run's final path before using `succeeded`.
6. Build `rwm_bindings.json` from live manager metadata and the complete
   `RUNS.tsv` inventory.
7. Run `validate-binding` before Stage 3 promotion.

Do not allocate one Idea per retry. Do not hide failed or cancelled Runs. Only
succeeded Runs may support a positive pilot claim.

An Idea is stable only while its primary contribution type and scientific object
remain stable. Implementation repair, hyperparameter changes, or a
hypothesis-preserving experimental revision use a new Attempt under the same
Idea. A change such as algorithm -> benchmark, cleaner -> diagnostic, reward
method -> evaluator, or system -> measurement protocol creates a **new Idea**
with a new Primary Contribution Contract. Never attach the component's success
to the original Idea.

Every calling-stage evidence row classifies its Run as
`prerequisite_evidence`, `component_validation`, `primary_claim_evidence`,
`discriminator_evidence`, `control_evidence`, or `integrity_evidence`. The
manager preserves identity and inventory; the independent reviewer sub-agent
judges whether the evidence really tests the frozen primary contribution. A
validator may only check that referenced Runs and files exist and belong to the
declared entities.

### 16.4 Stage 3 entity transaction

Stage 3 reuses the selected Idea and creates a new full-validation Attempt.
The pilot Attempt cannot be reused.

For each executable experiment configuration:

1. Allocate a Run before launching work.
2. Record the exact Run ID in the command and stage ledger.
3. Use the allocated scratch path for high-volume intermediates.
4. Use the allocated final path for exact config, command, audit logs, metrics,
   predictions needed for claims, figures/reports, and irreplaceable
   checkpoints.
5. Set the actual terminal status and preserve diagnostics for failures.
6. Update `rwm_binding.json` so its Run IDs exactly equal the manager catalog
   inventory for the Attempt.

One Run may support multiple preregistered matrix rows only when the stage ledger
records the exact mapping. A row-local `complete` flag has no authority.

### 16.5 Complete binding inventory

Every Attempt binding sets `complete_run_inventory: true` and lists every Run in
the live manager catalog exactly once. Each Run entry records:

- `run_id`
- `final_path`
- `required_status`: the Run's actual catalog status (`allocated`, `queued`,
  `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`)

`validate-binding` checks Project, Idea, Attempt, Run, catalog identity, status,
final path, durable artifacts, duplicates, omissions, and extra Runs. For
claim-supporting evidence, the calling stage applies the stricter rule that the
referenced Run must be `succeeded`.

### 16.6 Durable result and command receipt

Before a Run is marked `succeeded`, its final path must contain more than
`run.yaml`. At minimum persist:

- exact command and configuration;
- seed and revision identifiers;
- terminal exit/status record;
- metrics or evaluation output;
- logs needed to audit the result.

Calling stages maintain append-only command/run ledgers. The manager catalog is
the identity authority; the stage ledger is the scientific mapping authority.
Neither substitutes for the other.

### 16.7 Failure and resume behavior

- A helper non-zero exit blocks the transaction and is recorded verbatim.
- A network connector failure may trigger another legal source, but cannot
  bypass paper registration.
- A failed experiment retains its Run; a retry allocates a new Run.
- Resume begins by reading live catalogs and validating bindings.
- Never repair an inconsistency by deleting catalog history or copying an entity
  directory. Surface the mismatch and reconcile through the helper.

### 16.8 Stage acceptance boundary

The manager proves storage, identity, inventory, and durability. It does not
decide whether a literature corpus is deep enough, an idea is novel, an
experiment is adequate, or a claim is publishable. Auto Research must obtain
those independent scientific verdicts after manager validation.

## 17. Safety rules

- Never use `/`, `/home`, or `/data` for a new large model/dataset merely
  because the current working directory is there.
- Never use `/scratch` for the only copy of code, papers, final results,
  credentials, or irreplaceable checkpoints.
- Never delete a source until copy verification and compatibility-path checks
  pass.
- Never follow a compatibility symlink and then create a second physical copy.
- Never move a dirty Git repository as part of asset cleanup.
- Never expose the Hugging Face token or other credentials in logs/catalogs.
- Never assume a filename implies identical content; compare SHA-256 before
  deduplicating.
- Prefer XFS CoW reflinks over hardlinks for exact large-file deduplication so
  future writes remain isolated.
- Never create Idea, Attempt, or Run directories by hand when the manager
  helper can allocate them.
- Never encode lifecycle status by copying or renaming an Idea directory.
- Never put `test-tmp-*` trees inside durable project results.
- Never promote an Idea without a durable decision record and evidence links.

## 18. Invocation workflow

When this skill is invoked:

1. Run preflight.
2. Read `/data/results/README.md`.
3. Search all relevant catalogs using the task or asset query.
4. Detect the current persistent Project root.
5. If work creates a new Idea, Run, or PaperPackage, initialize/use the managed
   `.research/` tree and allocate IDs through `workspace_manager.py`.
6. Report reusable matches and their exact canonical paths.
7. Select persistent and ephemeral paths for the workflow.
8. Carry out the task while enforcing storage and lifecycle policy.
9. Update research and asset catalogs.
10. Confirm the Project, Idea, Attempt, Run or PaperPackage, scratch path when
    applicable, and durable result path used.

For Auto Research:

- Stage 1 is a managed Project inbox; always perform preflight and the complete
  paper-search/register transaction, but do not allocate an Idea merely for a
  broad opportunity map.
- Stage 2 allocates an Idea and pilot Attempt when a candidate enters executable
  validation; every executable pilot uses `create-run`.
- A discovered benchmark, evaluator, dataset, or other prerequisite that becomes
  a standalone contribution receives a new Idea and contract. Preserve lineage
  to the original Idea, but do not move or relabel its Runs as primary evidence
  for the original contribution.
- Stage 3 allocates a new validation Attempt under the selected Idea; every
  completed claim-critical matrix row maps to a succeeded manager Run with a
  durable result artifact.
- Stage 4 reuses the Stage 3 Idea and Attempt, registers the live venue
  resources, allocates one `PaperPackage`, and writes manuscript, review,
  audit, and Stage 5 handoff artifacts there. Writing revisions are snapshots
  inside the same package, not new Ideas, Attempts, or Runs.
- Stage 5 reuses the PaperPackage, performs independent technical review and
  adjudication, and creates new Attempts/Runs only for reviewer-approved
  experiments. It may mark the package `ready_for_submission`, but may not
  rewrite result history or hide material contradictory evidence.
- Use `validate-binding --binding-file <rwm_binding.json>` before a Stage 2 or
  Stage 3 success handoff. Stage-local JSON is not a substitute for live manager
  metadata and catalog entries.

If no argument is provided, return a concise environment summary and state
that the research workspace context is loaded.

## 6. Existing persistent workspaces

Keep these repositories at their current absolute locations:

- `/home/user/Agent-Related-Learning`

- `/home/user/AutoResearchClaw`

Do not relocate existing repositories or rewrite their internal asset paths
without a task-specific reason. Existing legacy paths are compatibility links

Place a new repository under:

`/home/user/research-workspaces/<topic>/<repository-name>`

Keep its virtual environment at:

`/home/user/research-workspaces/<topic>/<repository-name>/.venv`

Never clone repositories, install environments, or create code worktrees under
`/scratch` solely for speed. Script and import speed gains are negligible;

## 7. Canonical research entity model

Every managed research effort uses exactly four nested entities:

`Project -> Idea -> Attempt -> Run`

- **Project:** one durable code repository or workspace.
- **Idea:** one stable research hypothesis or direction. Never copy it into
  `idea_2`, `final-idea`, or another directory for a retry.
- **Attempt:** one implementation or methodological revision of an Idea.
- **Run:** one executable configuration, seed, or evaluation invocation.

Status belongs in metadata, not directory names.

### IDs

- Project: stable lowercase slug, for example `agent-evaluation`.
- Idea: `I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-slug`.
- Attempt: `ANNN-short-slug`.
- Run: `R-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` with optional collision suffix and optional `-s<seed>`.

Forbidden ad hoc names include `_2`, `final-final`, `attempt_new`,
`test-tmp-round4`, and status words encoded as directory copies.

## 8. Canonical project layout

Managed projects keep code and research control files on persistent storage:

```text
<project-root>/
├── src/
├── scripts/
├── configs/
├── tests/
├── third_party/
└── .research/
    ├── PROJECT.yaml
    ├── INDEX.tsv
    ├── inbox/
    ├── ideas/
    │   └── I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-slug/
    │       ├── idea.yaml
    │       ├── README.md
    │       ├── proposal/
    │       ├── literature/
    │       ├── plan/
    │       ├── reviews/
    │       │   ├── external/
    │       │   └── audits/
    │       ├── attempts/
    │       │   └── ANNN-short-slug/
    │       │       ├── attempt.yaml
    │       │       ├── implementation/
    │       │       ├── configs/
    │       │       └── runs/
    │       └── decision/
    ├── promoted/
    └── archive/
        ├── rejected/
        ├── paused/
        └── superseded/
```

The project root must remain on `/home/user` or `/data`, never on
`/scratch`.

Use the deterministic helper instead of manually inventing directories. `workspace_manager.py` serializes Idea/Attempt/Run allocation with the catalog lock and retries on collisions, so concurrent callers must use the helper rather than precomputing IDs:

```bash
MANAGER=/data/results/copilot-skills/research-workspace-manager/scripts/workspace_manager.py

python3 "$MANAGER" init-project \
  --root /absolute/persistent/project/path \
  --project project-slug

python3 "$MANAGER" create-idea \
  --root /absolute/persistent/project/path \
  --slug short-idea-slug \
  --title "Human-readable title"

python3 "$MANAGER" create-attempt \
  --idea /absolute/path/to/I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-idea-slug \
  --slug baseline

python3 "$MANAGER" create-run \
  --attempt /absolute/path/to/ANNN-baseline \
  --seed 13

python3 "$MANAGER" set-idea-status \
  --idea /absolute/path/to/I-YYYYMMDD-NNN-short-idea-slug \
  --status promoted

python3 "$MANAGER" set-attempt-status \
  --attempt /absolute/path/to/ANNN-baseline \
  --status evaluated

python3 "$MANAGER" set-run-status \
  --final /data/results/results/<project>/<idea>/<attempt>/<run> \
  --status succeeded

python3 "$MANAGER" summary --root /absolute/persistent/project/path
```


For Auto Research portfolio/GPU windows, derive deterministic sidecar window IDs with the stage-local helper:

```bash
python3 /data/results/copilot-skills/auto_research-stage-2-skill/scripts/portfolio_ledger.py window-id \
  --project-id <project> --idea-id <idea> --attempt-id <attempt> [--run-id <run>]
```

### Lifecycle states

Idea:

`inbox, scoped, planned, piloting, evaluating, promoted, rejected, paused, superseded`

Attempt:

`planned, implementing, running, evaluated, selected, rejected, paused`

Run:

`allocated, queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled`

Paper package:

`allocated, drafting, reviewing, ready_for_stage5, stage5_reviewing,
stage5_experimenting, stage5_revising, ready_for_submission, blocked_stage5,
failed, cancelled`

Retries create a new Attempt or Run, not a copied Idea directory.

## 9. Run storage contract

For each Run, the manager allocates:

```text
/scratch/assets/work/<project>/<idea>/<attempt>/<run>/
├── logs/
├── checkpoints/
├── predictions/
└── intermediate/

/data/results/results/<project>/<idea>/<attempt>/<run>/
├── run.yaml
├── reports/
├── figures/
└── final-checkpoint/
```

The Attempt's `runs/<run-id>` entry is a symbolic link to the persistent result
directory. The scratch path is recorded in `run.yaml`.

High-volume intermediate data belongs on scratch. Exact configuration, command,
seed, metrics, reports, figures, audit logs, and irreplaceable checkpoints must
be persisted under the result directory before a Run is complete.

## 10. Global research catalogs

The manager owns these persistent TSV catalogs:

- `/data/results/catalog/PROJECTS.tsv`
- `/data/results/catalog/IDEAS.tsv`
- `/data/results/catalog/ATTEMPTS.tsv`
- `/data/results/catalog/RUNS.tsv`

Do not edit them without acquiring
`/data/results/catalog/.catalog.lock`. Idea/Attempt/Run allocation also uses this lock plus collision retry to keep catalogs and directories consistent under concurrency. Prefer the manager helper for all
updates. These are indexes only; they must not duplicate payloads.

## 11. Legacy project handling

Existing trees may contain `ideaspark_run`, `phase0`, `phase1`, `attempt_1`,
`implementation`, `audit`, `review-stage`, `workspace/ideas`, or
`workspace/experiments`.

Do not reorganize a legacy tree merely because this skill was invoked. For new
work inside a legacy project:

1. Initialize `<project-root>/.research`.
2. Allocate the new Idea with the manager.
3. Link relevant legacy files from the managed Idea if needed.
4. Keep old phase directories unchanged until the user explicitly requests a
   migration.
5. During an approved migration, retain raw phase material under
   `<idea>/legacy/` and record its source path.

| Legacy | Managed structure |
|---|---|
| `ideaspark_run/<slug>` | `research/ideas/<idea-id>` |
| `phase0...phase4` | `proposal/`, `literature/`, `plan/`, or `legacy/` |
| `attempt_1` | `attempts/A001-*` |
| `implementation` | `attempts/<attempt>/implementation` |
| `review-stage`, `reviews` | `reviews/external` |
| `audit`, `audits` | `reviews/audits` |
| `test-tmp-*` | scratch temporary Run data |
| accepted paper work | promoted Idea plus persistent paper directory |

## 12. Placement rules for new assets

### Hugging Face

Use `HF_HOME=/scratch/assets/huggingface`. Do not pass a project-local
cache directory. If a tool requires `local_dir`, first verify that a cached
snapshot cannot be reused.

### Manual model download

Use:

`/scratch/assets/models/manual/<provider>/<model-name>`

Download to a sibling `.partial` path, validate size/checksum, then atomically
rename it. Never overwrite an existing model directory without checking its
revision and catalog record.

### Dataset

Use:

`/scratch/assets/datasets/<topic>/<dataset-name>`

Recommended topics include `tabular`, `text2sql`, `retrieval`, `agents`,
`coding`, `reasoning`, `multimodal`, and `benchmarks`.

### Derived cache

Use:

`/scratch/assets/caches/<cache-type>/<project-or-method>`

Examples of cache types: `experiments`, `models`, `retrieval`, `embeddings`,
`tokenized`, and `compiled`.

### Temporary experiment data

Use:

`/scratch/assets/work/<project>/<run-id>`

Use a stable run ID such as `<method>-<dataset>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>`.

## 13. Experiment output contract

For every substantial run, define both:

```bash
RUN_ID='<method>-<dataset>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>'
SCRATCH_RUN="/scratch/assets/work/<project>/$RUN_ID"
FINAL_RUN="/data/results/results/<project>/$RUN_ID"
```

Write high-volume temporary outputs and intermediate checkpoints to
`$SCRATCH_RUN`. Persist these to `$FINAL_RUN`:

- Exact configuration and command line
- Seeds and environment/package metadata
- Final metrics and evaluation outputs
- Logs needed to audit the result
- Plots, tables, reports, and paper-ready figures
- Best/final checkpoints that cannot be cheaply regenerated

Copy and verify final artifacts before deleting temporary data. During long
runs, sync an irreplaceable checkpoint after each major evaluation or epoch.
Never report an experiment complete while its only result copy is on
`/scratch`.

## 14. Paper management

Search `/data/results/catalog/PAPERS.tsv` by title, arXiv ID, DOI, and
topic before downloading. This is a per-paper requirement. Auto Research and
other calling skills must not reduce manager use to `init-project`.

Use the manager commands rather than manually appending catalog rows:

```bash
MANAGER=/data/results/copilot-skills/research-workspace-manager/scripts/workspace_manager.py

python3 "$MANAGER" paper-search --query '<title|doi|arxiv-id|topic>' --json

python3 "$MANAGER" register-paper \
  --source-pdf /scratch/assets/tmp/<run>/<paper>.pdf.partial \
```
